topics.title: Review of powers and integer indices

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(3^3\)

steps.explain: A positive integer power means repeated multiplication of the base. Here the base is 3 and the index is 3, so write three factors of 3.
Multiply step by step. First \(3 \times 3 = 9\), then multiply by the remaining factor.
Finish the product to evaluate the power.
So \(3^3 = 27\). This matches the option \(27\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(4^3\)

steps.explain: Write \(4^3\) as three factors of 4, because a positive integer index means repeated multiplication.
First multiply two factors: \(4 \times 4 = 16\).
Multiply by the last factor: \(16 \times 4 = 64\).
State the final simplified result. Therefore \(4^3 = 64\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(3^4\)

steps.explain: The index 4 means multiply the base 3 by itself four times.
Pair the multiplications: \(3 \times 3 = 9\) and another \(3 \times 3 = 9\).
Finish by multiplying the two nines together to get the value of the fourth power.
State the final simplified result. So \(3^4 = 81\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(2^5\)

steps.explain: Write out the five factors of 2 indicated by the index 5.
Build powers of 2 sequentially: \(2^2 = 4\), \(2^3 = 8\), \(2^4 = 16\).
One more doubling gives \(2^5\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. Therefore \(2^5 = 32\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(10^5\)

steps.explain: A power of 10 is 1 followed by as many zeros as the index. Here the index is 5.
Each factor of 10 adds one zero after 1.
Continue to five zeros after 1. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. So \(10^5 = 100000\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(7^2\)

steps.explain: Square means multiply the number by itself once: base 7, index 2.
Carry out the multiplication of the two equal factors to evaluate the square.
State the final simplified result. Therefore \(7^2 = 49\).

questions.stem: Write the number \(16\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: We need a prime base raised to a positive integer. Factor 16 into primes by repeated division by 2.
Continue until every factor is prime. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Count the factors of 2: there are 4, so write as a single power.
Index form with prime base: \(2^4\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(27\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Factor 27 using the prime 3 by repeated division until every factor is prime.
Three factors of 3 give index 3. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Prime-base index form is \(3^3\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(125\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Factor 125 by dividing by the prime 5. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Three factors of 5 give \(5^3\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. So the index form is \(5^3\).

questions.stem: Write the number \(243\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Factor 243 with prime 3: \(3^5 = 243\) because successive powers of 3 are 3, 9, 27, 81, 243.
State the final simplified result. Hence \(243 = 3^5\).

questions.stem: Write the number \(343\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Recognise 343 as a power of 7: \(7^2 = 49\).
Multiply by another 7: \(7^3 = 49 \times 7 = 343\).
So in prime-base index form, \(343 = 7^3\).

questions.stem: Write the number \(128\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Factor 128 by repeated division by 2 (it is a pure power of 2).
Continue: \(2^4 \times 8 = 2^5 \times 4 = 2^6 \times 2 = 2^7\).
Prime-base index form: \(2^7\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(\frac{1}{7}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: By definition, a negative index means the reciprocal of the positive power: \(a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}\).
Here the base is the prime 7 and the numerator is 1, so the index is \(-1\).
Index form with prime base: \(7^{-1}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(\frac{1}{25}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: First write the denominator as a prime power: \(25 = 5^2\).
So the fraction is the reciprocal of \(5^2\).
Apply the negative-index definition. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Prime-base index form: \(5^{-2}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(\frac{1}{11^3}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: The denominator is already a prime power \(11^3\).
The reciprocal of a positive power is the same base with a negative index.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(11^{-3}\).

questions.stem: Write the number \(\frac{1}{512}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Form the reciprocal. Using a^{-n} = 1/a^n converts the reciprocal of a prime power into prime-base index form.
Convert to a negative index. Using a^{-n} = 1/a^n converts the reciprocal of a prime power into prime-base index form.
Prime-base index form: \(2^{-9}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Write the number \(\frac{8}{128}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: Simplify the fraction first by dividing numerator and denominator by 8.
Write 16 as a prime power: \(16 = 2^4\).
Apply the negative-index law. Using a^{-n} = 1/a^n converts the reciprocal of a prime power into prime-base index form.
State the final simplified result. So \(\frac{8}{128} = 2^{-4}\).

questions.stem: Write the number \((169)^{-4}\) in index form with a prime number base.

steps.explain: First rewrite the composite base 169 as a prime square: \(169 = 13^2\).
Substitute into the given power. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Use the power-of-a-power law: multiply the indices \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\).
Prime-base index form: \(13^{-8}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: \(x^3y^2 \times x^5y^4\)

steps.explain: Multiply powers by adding indices for each base separately. Bases are \(x\) and \(y\).
Group like bases: \(x\)-powers together and \(y\)-powers together.
State the final simplified result. Simplified expression: \(x^8 y^6\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: \(u^3v^4 \times u^2v^5\)

steps.explain: Same-base product law for \(u\) and \(v\) separately.
Apply the product law separately to u and to v by adding matching indices.
Evaluate the sums the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(u^5 v^9\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: \(3x^5y^2 \times 5xy^4\)

steps.explain: Multiply coefficients and add indices for matching bases.
Multiply the numerical coefficients first, then prepare to add the indices of matching bases. Note that a lone x means x to the power 1.
Add the indices the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Simplified form: \(15x^6 y^6\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: \(4a^2b \times 6a^4b^3\)

steps.explain: Multiply numerical coefficients, then combine powers of \(a\) and of \(b\).
Multiply the numerical coefficients, then add the indices of a and of b separately.
Complete the sums the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(24a^6 b^4\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: \(2m^4n^5 \times 7m^3n^3\)

steps.explain: Multiply coefficients and add indices for \(m\) and \(n\).
Multiply the coefficients, then add the indices for m and for n.
Sum the indices the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Simplified: \(14m^7 n^8\).

questions.stem: Simplify the quotient, expressing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{a^3b^2}{a^2b^5}\)

steps.explain: For a quotient of powers with the same base, subtract indices: \(\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}\). Start with the given fraction.
Apply the quotient law to each base. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Rewrite any negative index as a positive index in the denominator: \(b^{-3} = \frac{1}{b^3}\).
Final simplified form with positive indices: \(\frac{a}{b^3}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the quotient, expressing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{40m^3n^5}{15mn^2}\)

steps.explain: Simplify the numerical coefficient and the powers separately.
Combine the coefficient and the variable powers into one neat fraction with positive indices only.
Answer with positive indices: \(\frac{8m^2 n^3}{3}\).

steps.explain: Subtract indices for each base in the quotient.

State the final simplified result. Simplified form: \(p^4 q^4\).

Combine the coefficient and the variable powers into one neat fraction with positive indices only.

questions.stem: Simplify the quotient, expressing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{15x^2y^4z^5}{25x^2y^6z^2}\)

steps.explain: Simplify coefficient and each base using the quotient law.
Use \(x^0 = 1\) and move \(y^{-2}\) to the denominator.
Final answer with positive indices: \(\frac{3z^3}{5y^2}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the quotient, expressing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{24a^4b^5c^7}{8b^8c^7}\)

questions.stem: Simplify: \((x^3y^2)^4\)

steps.explain: Power of a product: raise every factor inside the brackets to the outer index: \((ab)^n = a^n b^n\). Also \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\).
Multiply each inner index by 4. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Evaluate the products of indices. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. Simplified: \(x^{12} y^8\).

questions.stem: Simplify: \((m^4n^3)^5\)

steps.explain: Raise each factor inside to the power 5.
Use the power-of-a-power law: multiply every inner index by the outer index 5.
Compute the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(m^{20} n^{15}\).

questions.stem: Simplify: \((p^2q^3r^4s^5)^2\)

steps.explain: Distribute the outer index 2 to every base inside the brackets.
Multiply each index inside the brackets by the outer index 2 (power-of-a-power law).
Write the expanded product of powers. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Simplified form: \(p^4 q^6 r^8 s^{10}\).

questions.stem: Simplify: \((3x^4y)^3\)

steps.explain: The outer power applies to the coefficient as well as the pronumerals.
Compute \(3^3\) and multiply each letter index by 3. Note \(y = y^1\).
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(27x^{12} y^3\).

questions.stem: Simplify: \((4m^3n^5)^2\)

steps.explain: Raise the coefficient and each variable to the outer index 2.
Raise the coefficient 4 to the power 2, and multiply each letter index by 2.
Evaluate the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Simplified: \(16m^6 n^{10}\).

questions.stem: Simplify: \((2u^5v^3)^4\)

steps.explain: Distribute the outer power 4 to 2, \(u^5\) and \(v^3\).
Evaluate the numerical coefficient after the outer power has been applied to every factor.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(16u^{20} v^{12}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((2x^4)^3 \times 3x^5\)

steps.explain: First expand the power of a product: \((2x^4)^3 = 2^3 x^{12} = 8x^{12}\).
Now multiply the expanded term by 3x^5: multiply coefficients and add the powers of x.
Compute the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
Simplified form with positive index: \(24x^{17}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((3y^4)^2 \div (9y^5)\)

steps.explain: Expand the bracket first: \((3y^4)^2 = 9 y^8\).
Write as a fraction and cancel coefficients.
Apply the quotient law by subtracting the indices of y to finish the simplification.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(y^3\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(x^3y)^2}{xy^3} \times \frac{x^4y^6}{xy}\)

steps.explain: Expand the squared bracket in the first numerator: \((x^3 y)^2 = x^6 y^2\).
Simplify each fraction using the quotient law.
Multiply: add indices for \(x\) and for \(y\).
Final answer with positive indices: \(x^8 y^4\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{a^5b^3}{ab^4} \div \frac{(ab^3)^2}{a^4b^7}\)

steps.explain: Division of fractions means multiply by the reciprocal. First expand \((ab^3)^2 = a^2 b^6\).
steps.work: \(\frac{a^5 b^3}{a b^4} \div \frac{a^2 b^6}{a^4 b^7} = \frac{a^5 b^3}{a b^4} \times \frac{a^4 b^7}{a^2 b^6}\)

steps.explain: Simplify the first fraction: \(a^{5-1} b^{3-4} = a^4 b^{-1}\). Second: \(a^{4-2} b^{7-6} = a^2 b\).
State the final simplified result. Simplified form: \(a^6\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{x^5y^7}{(xy^3)^2} \times \frac{x^4y^2}{x^3y}\)

steps.explain: Expand the bracket: \((x y^3)^2 = x^2 y^6\).
Simplify each quotient: first gives \(x^{3} y^{1}\); second gives \(x^{1} y^{1}\).
Multiply the results the algebraic expression carefully so each index law is applied exactly once and no intermediate factor is dropped.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(x^4 y^2\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(m^3n)^2}{mn^4} \div \frac{mn}{(m^3n)^2}\)

steps.explain: Expand both squared brackets: \((m^3 n)^2 = m^6 n^2\). Division becomes multiplication by the reciprocal.
steps.work: \(\frac{m^6 n^2}{m n^4} \div \frac{m n}{m^6 n^2} = \frac{m^6 n^2}{m n^4} \times \frac{m^6 n^2}{m n}\)

steps.explain: Simplify each part: first \(m^{5} n^{-2}\); second \(m^{5} n^{1}\).
Add indices: \(m^{10} n^{-1}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Final form with positive indices: \(\frac{m^{10}}{n}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(3^{-1}\)

steps.explain: By definition, a negative index is the reciprocal of the positive power: \(a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}\).
Since \(3^1 = 3\), the value is the reciprocal of 3.
Evaluated value: \(\frac{1}{3}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(4^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Write the negative power as a reciprocal of a positive power.
Evaluate the denominator: \(4^2 = 16\). This replaces the power with its ordinary integer value.
State the final simplified result. So \(4^{-2} = \frac{1}{16}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(5^{-1}\)

steps.explain: Apply the negative-index definition. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(5^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Convert the negative index to a reciprocal.
Square the base: \(5^2 = 25\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. Therefore \(5^{-2} = \frac{1}{25}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(10^{-4}\)

steps.explain: Write as a reciprocal of a positive power of 10.
A power of 10 is 1 followed by that many zeros: \(10^4 = 10000\).
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(\frac{1}{10000}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{-1}\)

steps.explain: A fraction to the power \(-1\) is simply its reciprocal: \(\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{-1} = \frac{b}{a}\).
No further simplification is needed. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Evaluated value: \(\frac{6}{5}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\left(\frac{12}{11}\right)^{-1}\)

steps.explain: Flip the fraction for the index \(-1\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

State the final simplified result. Answer: \(\frac{11}{12}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-3}\)

steps.explain: For a negative outer index, take the reciprocal of the fraction first, then raise to the positive power: \(\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{n}\).
Raise numerator and denominator to the power 3.
Evaluated value: \(\frac{27}{8}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Flip the fraction and change the index to positive 2.

State the final simplified result. Answer: \(\frac{16}{9}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-4}\)

steps.explain: Reciprocal then positive power. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

Evaluated value: \(\frac{625}{16}\). Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(2^{-5}\)

Compute \(2^5 = 32\). This replaces the power with its ordinary integer value.
State the final simplified result. So \(2^{-5} = \frac{1}{32}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(7 + x^0\), where \(x \neq 0\).

steps.explain: Any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1: \(x^0 = 1\) when \(x \neq 0\).
Replace x^0 with 1 in the expression 7 + x^0.
Add the constant 7 to 1 to obtain the final numerical value.
State the final simplified result. Value: \(8\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \(\frac{6x^0}{(7y)^0}\), where \(x, y \neq 0\).

steps.explain: Zero-index law: any non-zero base to the power 0 is 1. So \(x^0 = 1\) and \((7y)^0 = 1\).
Replace each zero-power factor with 1 inside the fraction.
The fraction then reduces to the constant 6 over 1.
State the final simplified result. Value: \(6\).

questions.stem: Evaluate: \((3 + x)^0\), where \(x \neq -3\).

steps.explain: The zero-index law says that any non-zero quantity raised to the power 0 equals 1.
The condition \(x \neq -3\) ensures the base is not zero, so the law applies.
Therefore the expression evaluates to 1.

questions.stem: Evaluate: \((5^4)^0\)

steps.explain: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 is 1. Here the base is \(5^4\), which is not zero.
Apply the zero-index law directly: any non-zero base to the power 0 equals 1.
State the final simplified result. Final value: 1.

steps.explain: A power of \(-1\) means take the reciprocal of everything inside the brackets.

Multiply the coefficients. Apply the index law for multiplication: add the indices for terms with the same base.
Simplify the calculations and write the final answer with positive indices.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((p^{-3}q^2)^5 \times (p^{-4}q^3)^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Expand each bracket by multiplying indices by the outer power.
Multiply the expanded forms: add indices for each base.
Write the negative power of \(p\) in the denominator.
State the final simplified result. Final form: \(\frac{q^4}{p^7}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\left(\frac{a^3b^{-2}}{c^5}\right)^{-3}\)

steps.explain: A negative outer index means take the reciprocal and raise to the positive power, or multiply every index by \(-3\).
Rewrite: a negative index in the denominator becomes a positive power in the numerator, and vice versa.
Answer with positive indices: \(\frac{b^6 c^{15}}{a^9}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\left(\frac{x^{-2}y^3}{z^{-3}}\right)^{-4}\)

steps.explain: Start with the given algebraic fraction raised to a power.
Apply the power outside the bracket to both the numerator and the denominator.
Multiply the indices for every term in the numerator and denominator.
Simplify the calculations and write the final answer with positive indices.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{3x^{-2}y^3}{x^4y^{-3}} \times \frac{5x^5y^{-2}}{10xy^{-4}}\)

steps.explain: Simplify the first fraction: coefficients stay, subtract indices.
Simplify the second fraction: coefficient \(\frac{5}{10} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Multiply the two simplified results. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Write with positive indices: \(\frac{3 y^8}{2 x^2}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{a^3b^{-4}}{a^5b^3} \times \frac{(ab^3)^{-2}}{a^3b^5}\)

steps.explain: Start with the multiplication of algebraic fractions.
Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together.
Simplify the calculations and write the final answer with positive indices.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{a^5b^{-2}}{(a^3b)^{-2}} \div \frac{a^2b^3}{(ab)^{-3}}\)

steps.explain: Expand the brackets with negative outer powers: \((a^3 b)^{-2} = a^{-6} b^{-2}\) and \((ab)^{-3} = a^{-3} b^{-3}\).
For division of powers with the same base, subtract the indices (watch the signs of negative indices).
State the final simplified result. Final form: \(\frac{a^6}{b^6}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{x^{-5}y^3}{(xy^2)^{-4}} \div \frac{(xy)^{-2}}{x^2y^4}\)

steps.explain: Expand the powered brackets: \((xy^2)^{-4} = x^{-4} y^{-8}\) and \((xy)^{-2} = x^{-2} y^{-2}\).
Simplify the first fraction using the quotient law.
Simplify the second fraction, then divide (multiply by reciprocal).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(3x^3y^{-4})^2}{z^3} \times \frac{(3^2x^{-2}y^3)^{-1}}{z^2}\)

steps.explain: Start with the multiplication of algebraic fractions.
Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together.
Simplify the calculations and write the final answer with positive indices.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(a^3b^2)^3}{c^{-4}} \times (a^2bc^{-3})^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Expand the first part: \((a^3 b^2)^3 = a^9 b^6\), and \(\frac{1}{c^{-4}} = c^4\). Expand the second: \((a^2 b c^{-3})^{-2} = a^{-4} b^{-2} c^{6}\).
Add the indices for each base separately after every bracket has been expanded.
All indices are positive already. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(a^5 b^4 c^{10}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(x^3)^4}{y^4} \div \left(\frac{x^2}{y^3}\right)^{-3}\)

steps.explain: Simplify the first part: \((x^3)^4 = x^{12}\), so the first fraction is \(\frac{x^{12}}{y^4}\). Expand the second: \(\left(\frac{x^2}{y^3}\right)^{-3} = \frac{x^{-6}}{y^{-9}}\).
Division: multiply by the reciprocal. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
State the final simplified result. Final form: \(\frac{x^{18}}{y^{13}}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{(3x^5)^3}{y^8} \div \frac{(x^3)^{-2}}{3y^2}\)

steps.explain: Expand the first numerator: \((3x^5)^3 = 27 x^{15}\). Second: \((x^3)^{-2} = x^{-6}\).
Multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
Multiply: coefficient \(27 \times 3 = 81\); indices \(x^{15-(-6)} = x^{21}\), \(y^{2-8} = y^{-6}\).
State the final simplified result. Answer: \(\frac{81x^{21}}{y^6}\).
Rewrite every negative power as a reciprocal, and evaluate the positive powers in the denominator.
Add the fractions in the numerator using a common denominator of 4. Simplify the denominator.
Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by \(\frac{1}{6}\).
Cancel the common numerical factor in the numerator and denominator to reach lowest terms.
State the final simplified result. Final value: \(\frac{1}{8}\).
Convert negative powers to unit fractions and evaluate the positive powers.
Numerator: common denominator 27 gives \(\frac{9}{27} + \frac{1}{27} = \frac{10}{27}\). Denominator: \(3 + 27 = 30\).
Rewrite the complex fraction as a product.
Simplify by dividing numerator and denominator by 10.
State the final simplified result. Final value: \(\frac{1}{81}\).
Rewrite negative powers as fractions and evaluate positive powers.
Numerator: \(\frac{9}{27} - \frac{1}{27} = \frac{8}{27}\). Denominator: \(3 - 27 = -24\).
Multiply by the reciprocal of the denominator.
Simplify by dividing numerator and denominator by 8.
State the final simplified result. Final value: \(-\frac{1}{81}\).
Convert each negative power in the numerator to a unit fraction, and expand the positive powers in the denominator.
Numerator with common denominator 27: \(\frac{9 + 3 + 1}{27} = \frac{13}{27}\). Denominator: \(3 + 9 + 27 = 39\).
Rewrite as a single fraction product. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
Note that \(27 \times 39 = 27 \times 3 \times 13 = 81 \times 13\), so the factor 13 cancels.
State the final simplified result. Final value: \(\frac{1}{81}\).

questions.stem: If \(n = 2\), find the value of \(2^n + 2^{3-n} + 2^{n-4}\).

steps.explain: Substitute the given value \(n = 2\) into every exponent.
Simplify the exponents: \(3-2 = 1\) and \(2-4 = -2\).
Add the integers first, then combine with the fraction using a common denominator of 4.
State the final simplified result. Final value: \(\frac{25}{4}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{a - b^{-1}}{a^{-1} - b}\)

steps.explain: Rewrite every negative index as a unit fraction so the expression is ordinary rational arithmetic.
Combine terms over a common denominator in the numerator and in the denominator.
Notice that \(1 - ab = -(ab - 1)\), so the factors \((ab - 1)\) cancel with a sign change.
Simplified form with positive indices: \(-\frac{a}{b}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((m^{-1} + n^{-1})(m^{-1} - n^{-1})\)

steps.explain: This is a difference of squares pattern: \((X + Y)(X - Y) = X^2 - Y^2\) with \(X = m^{-1}\) and \(Y = n^{-1}\).
Rewrite negative powers as unit fractions.
Combine over the common denominator \(m^2 n^2\).
Final form with positive indices: \(\frac{n^2 - m^2}{m^2 n^2}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{4ab}{a^{-1} + b^{-1}}\)

steps.explain: Rewrite the negative indices in the denominator as unit fractions.
Combine the denominator over a common denominator \(ab\).
Dividing by a fraction means multiply by its reciprocal.
Simplified form: \(\frac{4a^2 b^2}{a + b}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \(\frac{p^{-1} + q^{-1}}{p^{-2} + q^{-2}}\)

steps.explain: Rewrite every negative index as a unit fraction.
Combine numerator and denominator separately.
steps.work: \(\frac{\frac{q + p}{pq}}{\frac{q^2 + p^2}{p^2 q^2}} = \frac{p + q}{pq} \times \frac{p^2 q^2}{p^2 + q^2}\)

steps.explain: Cancel one factor of \(p\) and one factor of \(q\).
steps.work: \(\frac{(p + q) \cdot p q}{p^2 + q^2} = \frac{pq(p + q)}{p^2 + q^2}\)

steps.explain: Final form: \(\frac{pq(p + q)}{p^2 + q^2}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((a^{-1} + b)^{-2}\)

steps.explain: Rewrite \(a^{-1}\) as a unit fraction inside the brackets.
Combine over a common denominator. Keep every intermediate power written clearly so the next index-law step is unambiguous.
A negative outer power means take the reciprocal and square: \(\left(\frac{A}{B}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{B}{A}\right)^{2}\).
Simplified form: \(\frac{a^2}{(1 + ab)^2}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the expression, writing each pronumeral in the answer with a positive index: \((m^{-2} + n^{-3})^{-1}\)

steps.explain: Rewrite each negative power as a unit fraction.
Combine the sum over the common denominator \(m^2 n^3\).
The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction flipped.
Final form with positive indices: \(\frac{m^2 n^3}{n^3 + m^2}\).

questions.stem: The numbers \(A=5.6\times10^{-2}\), \(B=0.93\times10^{-1}\) and \(C=71\times10^{-3}\), listed in ascending order, is:
